sanskrit: jaritārir uvāca purataḥ kṛcchrakālasya dhīmāñ jāgarti pūruṣaḥ sa kṛcchrakālaṃ saṃprāpya vyathāṃ naivaiti karhi cit
english: Jaritāri said: A wise man stays vigilant before a time of peril arrives; having thus foreseen the time of peril, he does not suffer anguish at any moment when it comes.

sanskrit: yas tu kṛcchram asaṃprāptaṃ vicetā nāvabudhyate sa kṛcchrakāle vyathito na prajānāti kiṃ cana
english: But the witless one who does not perceive the peril before it arrives — when the time of peril comes, he is overwhelmed with distress and cannot comprehend anything at all.

sanskrit: sārisṛkva uvāca dhīras tvam asi medhāvī prāṇakṛcchram idaṃ ca naḥ śūraḥ prājño bahūnāṃ hi bhavaty eko na saṃśayaḥ
english: Sārisṛkva said: You are steadfast and intelligent; and this is indeed a crisis for our very lives. Truly, a single brave and wise man becomes the support of many — there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: stambamitra uvāca jyeṣṭhas trātā bhavati vai jyeṣṭho muñcati kṛcchrataḥ jyeṣṭhaś cen na prajānāti kanīyān kiṃ kariṣyati
english: Stambamitra said: It is indeed the eldest who becomes the protector; the eldest rescues from danger. But if the eldest does not understand, what can the younger ones do?

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca hiraṇyaretās tvarito jvalann āyāti naḥ kṣayam saptajihvo 'nalaḥ kṣāmo lelihānopasarpati
english: Droṇa said: He of golden seed comes swiftly blazing toward our destruction; the seven-tongued fire, lean and licking with his flames, is creeping close upon us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto bhrātṛbhis tu jaritārir vibhāvasum tuṣṭāva prāñjalir bhūtvā yathā tac chṛṇu pārthiva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by his brothers, Jaritāri praised Vibhāvasu, the fire, with joined palms. Hear how he did so, O king.

sanskrit: jaritārir uvāca ātmāsi vāyoḥ pavanaḥ śarīram uta vīrudhām yonir āpaś ca te śukra yonis tvam asi cāmbhasaḥ
english: Jaritāri said: You are the very self of the wind; the wind is your body. You are the womb of all herbs and plants. O pure one, the waters too are your source; you are the womb of the waters.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ cādhaś ca gacchanti visarpanti ca pārśvataḥ arciṣas te mahāvīrya raśmayaḥ savitur yathā
english: Your flames, O greatly mighty one, rise upward and descend downward and spread out on every side — even as the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: sārisṛkva uvāca mātā prapannā pitaraṃ na vidmaḥ; pakṣāś ca no na prajātābjaketo na nas trātā vidyate 'gne tvad anyas; tasmād dhi naḥ parirakṣaikavīra
english: Sārisṛkva said: Our mother has fled to our father; we do not know him. Our wings have not yet grown, O lotus-bannered one. There is no protector for us other than you, O Fire. Therefore do you alone guard us, O sole hero.

sanskrit: yad agne te śivaṃ rūpaṃ ye ca te sapta hetayaḥ tena naḥ parirakṣādya īḍitaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Whatever benign form you have, O Agni, and whatever are your seven weapons — with that protect us today, O praised one, for we seek your shelter.

sanskrit: tvam evaikas tapase jātavedo; nānyas taptā vidyate goṣu deva ṛṣīn asmān bālakān pālayasva; pareṇāsmān praihi vai havyavāha
english: You alone, O Jātavedas, are the one who blazes for austerity; no other scorcher is found among living beings, O divine one. Protect us who are sages and children. Pass beyond us, O carrier of oblations.

sanskrit: stambamitra uvāca sarvam agne tvam evaikas tvayi sarvam idaṃ jagat tvaṃ dhārayasi bhūtāni bhuvanaṃ tvaṃ bibharṣi ca
english: Stambamitra said: You alone are everything, O Agni; in you exists all this universe. You sustain all living beings; you uphold the entire world.

sanskrit: tvam agnir havyavāhas tvaṃ tvam eva paramaṃ haviḥ manīṣiṇas tvāṃ yajante bahudhā caikadhaiva ca
english: You are Agni the carrier of oblations; you yourself are also the supreme oblation. The wise ones worship you in many ways and also as a single unity.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭvā lokāṃs trīn imān havyavāha; prāpte kāle pacasi punaḥ samiddhaḥ sarvasyāsya bhuvanasya prasūtis; tvam evāgne bhavasi punaḥ pratiṣṭhā
english: Having created these three worlds, O carrier of oblations, when the time comes you blaze up and cook them again. You are the primal source of this entire universe; you, O Agni, again become its foundation.

sanskrit: tvam annaṃ prāṇināṃ bhuktam antarbhūto jagatpate nityaṃ pravṛddhaḥ pacasi tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: You are the food consumed by all living beings; dwelling within them, O lord of the universe, you perpetually grow and digest it. In you everything is established.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca sūryo bhūtvā raśmibhir jātavedo; bhūmer ambho bhūmijātān rasāṃś ca viśvān ādāya punar utsargakāle; sṛṣṭvā vṛṣṭyā bhāvayasīha śukra
english: Droṇa said: Becoming the sun with your rays, O Jātavedas, you draw up from the earth its waters and all the essences of what is born from the earth; then at the time of release, creating rain, you nourish all, O pure one.

sanskrit: tvatta etāḥ punaḥ śukra vīrudho haritacchadāḥ jāyante puṣkariṇyaś ca samudraś ca mahodadhiḥ
english: From you, O pure one, these green-leafed plants are born anew; from you spring the lotus pools, the ocean, and the great sea.

sanskrit: idaṃ vai sadma tigmāṃśo varuṇasya parāyaṇam śivas trātā bhavāsmākaṃ māsmān adya vināśaya
english: This is indeed the abode and ultimate refuge of Varuṇa, O sharp-rayed one. Be our auspicious protector; do not destroy us today.

sanskrit: piṅgākṣa lohitagrīva kṛṣṇavartman hutāśana pareṇa praihi muñcāsmān sāgarasya gṛhān iva
english: O tawny-eyed one, O red-throated one, O one whose path is black, O devourer of offerings — pass beyond us and release us, as one releases the dwellers of the ocean.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto jātavedā droṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā droṇam āha pratītātmā mandapālapratijñayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Droṇa of effortless deeds, Jātavedas, confident by virtue of Mandapāla's promise, spoke to Droṇa.

sanskrit: ṛṣir droṇas tvam asi vai brahmaitad vyāhṛtaṃ tvayā īpsitaṃ te kariṣyāmi na ca te vidyate bhayam
english: Fire said: You are truly the sage Droṇa; what you have spoken is the sacred word of Brahman itself. I shall do what you desire, and you need have no fear.

sanskrit: mandapālena yūyaṃ hi mama pūrvaṃ niveditāḥ varjayeḥ putrakān mahyaṃ dahan dāvam iti sma ha
english: Indeed, you were presented to me beforehand by Mandapāla, who said: "Spare my little sons for my sake when burning the forest."

sanskrit: yac ca tad vacanaṃ tasya tvayā yac ceha bhāṣitam ubhayaṃ me garīyas tad brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te bhṛśaṃ prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te brahman stotreṇa te vibho
english: Both that word of his and what you have spoken here — both together weigh heavily with me. Tell me what I shall do for you. I am greatly pleased; good fortune to you, O brahmin, for your hymn, O lord.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca ime mārjārakāḥ śukra nityam udvejayanti naḥ etān kuruṣva daṃṣṭrāsu havyavāha sabāndhavān
english: Droṇa said: These cats, O pure one, ever torment us. Take them and their kin in your jaws, O carrier of oblations.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tat kṛtavān vahnir abhyanujñāya śārṅgakān dadāha khāṇḍavaṃ caiva samiddho janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The fire did as asked; having granted leave to the śārṅga birds, he blazed up and burned the Khāṇḍava forest, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mandapālo 'pi kauravya cintayānaḥ sutāṃs tadā uktavān apy aśītāṃśuṃ naiva sa sma na tapyate
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Mandapāla too, O descendant of Kuru, was thinking anxiously about his sons at that time; and though he had spoken to the fire himself, he was not without anguish.

sanskrit: sa tapyamānaḥ putrārthe lapitām idam abravīt kathaṃ nv aśaktāḥ plavane lapite mama putrakāḥ
english: Burning with worry for the sake of his sons, he said to Lapitā: "How are my little sons, who cannot yet fly, faring now?"

sanskrit: vardhamāne hutavahe vāte śīghraṃ pravāyati asamarthā vimokṣāya bhaviṣyanti mamātmajāḥ
english: "With the oblation-carrier fire growing and the wind blowing swiftly, my children will be unable to escape."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nv aśaktā trāṇāya mātā teṣāṃ tapasvinī bhaviṣyaty asukhāviṣṭā putratrāṇam apaśyatī
english: "How will their wretched mother, unable to protect them, be seized with misery, seeing no means to save her sons?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu saraṇe 'śaktān patane ca mamātmajān saṃtapyamānā abhito vāśamānābhidhāvatī
english: "How will she, burning with grief and crying out on all sides, run toward my children who are unable to flee or fly away?"

sanskrit: jaritāriḥ kathaṃ putraḥ sārisṛkvaḥ kathaṃ ca me stambamitraḥ kathaṃ droṇaḥ kathaṃ sā ca tapasvinī
english: "How fares my son Jaritāri? How does Sārisṛkva fare? How does Stambamitra fare? How does Droṇa fare? And how does that wretched one fare?"

sanskrit: lālapyamānaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ mandapālaṃ tathā vane lapitā pratyuvācedaṃ sāsūyam iva bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the sage Mandapāla lamented thus in the forest, Lapitā replied to him with words that seemed to carry a note of jealousy, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na te suteṣv avekṣāsti tān ṛṣīn uktavān asi tejasvino vīryavanto na teṣāṃ jvalanād bhayam
english: Lapitā said: You have no real concern for your sons. You yourself said to those sages: "They are full of energy and might; they have no fear from the fire."

sanskrit: tathāgnau te parīttāś ca tvayā hi mama saṃnidhau pratiśrutaṃ tathā ceti jvalanena mahātmanā
english: Moreover, they were entrusted by you to the fire, and in my very presence the great-souled fire promised accordingly.

sanskrit: lokapālo 'nṛtāṃ vācaṃ na tu vaktā kathaṃ cana samarthās te ca vaktāro na te teṣv asti mānasam
english: A guardian of the worlds can never speak an untruth under any circumstances. And your sons are capable of speaking for themselves. Your mind, however, is not with them.

sanskrit: tām eva tu mamāmitrīṃ cintayan paritapyase dhruvaṃ mayi na te sneho yathā tasyāṃ purābhavat
english: It is that rival of mine that you are thinking of and tormenting yourself about. Surely you have no affection for me as you once had for her.

sanskrit: na hi pakṣavatā nyāyyaṃ niḥsnehena suhṛjjane pīḍyamāna upadraṣṭuṃ śaktenātmā kathaṃ cana
english: For it is not proper for one who has wings to watch indifferently while one who loves him suffers, especially when he has the power to help.

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ jaritām eva yadarthaṃ paritapyase cariṣyāmy aham apy ekā yathā kāpuruṣe tathā
english: Go to Jaritā herself, for whom you are tormenting yourself. I too shall wander alone, as one does in the case of a coward.

sanskrit: mandapāla uvāca nāham evaṃ care loke yathā tvam abhimanyase apatyahetor vicare tac ca kṛcchragataṃ mama
english: Mandapāla said: I do not move about in the world as you imagine. I wander on account of my children — and that situation is fraught with difficulty for me.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ hitvā bhaviṣye 'rthe yo 'valambeta mandadhīḥ avamanyeta taṃ loko yathecchasī tathā kuru
english: The dull-witted one who abandons what is present to cling to what is merely future — the world would hold him in contempt. Do as you wish.

sanskrit: eṣa hi jvalamāno 'gnir lelihāno mahīruhān dveṣyaṃ hi hṛdi saṃtāpaṃ janayaty aśivaṃ mama
english: For this blazing fire, licking up the great trees, generates in my heart an inauspicious and hateful anguish.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmād deśād atikrānte jvalane jaritā tataḥ jagāma putrakān eva tvaritā putragṛddhinī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After the fire had passed beyond that region, Jaritā, full of longing for her little ones, quickly rushed toward her children.

sanskrit: sā tān kuśalinaḥ sarvān nirmuktāñ jātavedasaḥ rorūyamāṇā kṛpaṇā sutān dṛṣṭavatī vane
english: She found all of them safe and sound in the forest, freed from Jātavedas, and she saw her sons weeping piteously.

sanskrit: aśraddheyatamaṃ teṣāṃ darśanaṃ sā punaḥ punaḥ ekaikaśaś ca tān putrān krośamānānvapadyata
english: Finding their sight almost too wonderful to believe, she went to each of her crying sons one by one, again and again.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyagacchat sahasā mandapālo 'pi bhārata atha te sarva evainaṃ nābhyanandanta vai sutāḥ
english: Then Mandapāla also came quickly, O Bhārata. But all his sons did not greet him with joy.

sanskrit: lālapyamānam ekaikaṃ jaritāṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ nocus te vacanaṃ kiṃ cit tam ṛṣiṃ sādhv asādhu vā
english: Though he lamented to each of them one by one and to Jaritā again and again, they did not speak a single word to that sage — neither kind nor harsh.

sanskrit: mandapāla uvāca jyeṣṭhaḥ sutas te katamaḥ katamas tadanantaraḥ madhyamaḥ katamaḥ putraḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ katamaś ca te
english: Mandapāla said: Which is your eldest son? Which comes after him? Which son is the middle one? And which is your youngest?

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantaṃ duḥkhārtaṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase kṛtavān asmi havyāśe naiva śāntim ito labhe
english: Why do you not respond to me as I speak in distress? I made a pact with the fire-eater; and yet I find no peace here.

sanskrit: jaritovāca kiṃ te jyeṣṭhe sute kāryaṃ kim anantajena vā kiṃ ca te madhyame kāryaṃ kiṃ kaniṣṭhe tapasvini
english: Jaritā said: What business do you have with the eldest son? Or with the one who comes after him? What business do you have with the middle one, or with the youngest, you wretched man?

sanskrit: yas tvaṃ māṃ sarvaśo hīnām utsṛjyāsi gataḥ purā tām eva lapitāṃ gaccha taruṇīṃ cāruhāsinīm
english: You who abandoned me utterly and went away before — go back to that young Lapitā with her lovely smile.

sanskrit: mandapāla uvāca na strīṇāṃ vidyate kiṃ cid anyatra puruṣāntarāt sāpatnakam ṛte loke bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā
english: Mandapāla said: For women there is nothing at all besides another man. Rivalry between co-wives is inescapable — it must be so in the world.

sanskrit: suvratāpi hi kalyāṇī sarvalokapariśrutā arundhatī paryaśaṅkad vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam
english: Even the virtuous and beautiful Arundhatī, renowned throughout all the worlds, suspected Vasiṣṭha, the greatest of sages.

sanskrit: viśuddhabhāvam atyantaṃ sadā priyahite ratam saptarṣimadhyagaṃ vīram avamene ca taṃ munim
english: She despised that utterly pure-hearted sage, ever devoted to her welfare and benefit, that hero dwelling among the seven sages.

sanskrit: apadhyānena sā tena dhūmāruṇasamaprabhā lakṣyālakṣyā nābhirūpā nimittam iva lakṣyate
english: Through that suspicion, her radiance became like smoky red; she can be barely seen, dim and without her former beauty — she is perceived now only as a pale mark.

sanskrit: apatyahetoḥ saṃprāptaṃ tathā tvam api mām iha iṣṭam evaṃgate hitvā sā tathaiva ca vartase
english: I came here for the sake of offspring, and so you too are now forsaking the beloved and acting in the same way.

sanskrit: naiva bhāryeti viśvāsaḥ kāryaḥ puṃsā kathaṃ cana na hi kāryam anudhyāti bhāryā putravatī satī
english: A man should never place total trust in a wife, for a wife who is a true mother of sons does not think of a husband's duty.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te sarva evainaṃ putrāḥ samyag upāsire sa ca tān ātmajān rājann āśvāsayitum ārabhat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all his sons attended upon him properly, and he began to comfort his children, O king.

sanskrit: mandapāla uvāca yuṣmākaṃ parirakṣārthaṃ vijñapto jvalano mayā agninā ca tathety evaṃ pūrvam eva pratiśrutam
english: Mandapāla said: For the sake of protecting you I petitioned the fire, and the fire promised accordingly — "So be it" — even before this.

sanskrit: agner vacanam ājñāya mātur dharmajñatāṃ ca vaḥ yuṣmākaṃ ca paraṃ vīryaṃ nāhaṃ pūrvam ihāgataḥ
english: Knowing the word of the fire, your mother's knowledge of dharma, and your own supreme valor, I did not come here sooner.

sanskrit: na saṃtāpo hi vaḥ kāryaḥ putrakā maraṇaṃ prati ṛṣīn veda hutāśo 'pi brahma tad viditaṃ ca vaḥ
english: You should not grieve over death, my dear children. Even the fire knows the sages and the sacred knowledge of Brahman; and you too understand this.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam āśvāsya putrān sa bhāryāṃ cādāya bhārata mandapālas tato deśād anyaṃ deśaṃ jagāma ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted his sons and taking his wife with him, O Bhārata, Mandapāla departed from that place to another region.

sanskrit: bhagavān api tigmāṃśuḥ samiddhaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ vanam dadāha saha kṛṣṇābhyāṃ janayañ jagato 'bhayam
english: The divine sharp-rayed fire also burned the blazing Khāṇḍava forest together with the two Kṛṣṇas, generating fearlessness for the world.

sanskrit: vasāmedovahāḥ kulyās tatra pītvā ca pāvakaḥ agacchat paramāṃ tṛptiṃ darśayām āsa cārjunam
english: Drinking streams of fat and marrow flowing there, the purifying fire attained supreme satisfaction and revealed himself to Arjuna.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣād bhagavān avatīrya sureśvaraḥ marudgaṇavṛtaḥ pārthaṃ mādhavaṃ cābravīd idam
english: Then the lord of the gods, surrounded by the hosts of Maruts, descended from the sky and spoke these words to Pārtha and to Mādhava.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ yuvābhyāṃ karmedam amarair api duṣkaram varān vṛṇītaṃ tuṣṭo 'smi durlabhān apy amānuṣān
english: Indra said: You two have accomplished a feat difficult even for the immortals. Choose your boons — I am pleased; choose even those that are rare and beyond human reach.

sanskrit: pārthas tu varayām āsa śakrād astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ grahītuṃ tac ca śakro 'sya tadā kālaṃ cakāra ha
english: Pārtha then chose from Śakra to receive all weapons in full; and Śakra set a proper time for granting them to him.

sanskrit: yadā prasanno bhagavān mahādevo bhaviṣyati tubhyaṃ tadā pradāsyāmi pāṇḍavāstrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: Indra said: When the divine Mahādeva shall be graciously disposed toward you, then I will grant you all the weapons of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: aham eva ca taṃ kālaṃ vetsyāmi kurunandana tapasā mahatā cāpi dāsyāmi tava tāny aham
english: I myself will know that moment, O delight of the Kurus; and through great austerity I too shall grant those weapons to you.

sanskrit: āgneyāni ca sarvāṇi vāyavyāni tathaiva ca madīyāni ca sarvāṇi grahīṣyasi dhanaṃjaya
english: All the weapons of Agni, all those of Vāyu as well, and all those that are mine — all of these you shall receive, O Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'pi jagrāha prītiṃ pārthena śāśvatīm dadau ca tasmai devendras taṃ varaṃ prītimāṃs tadā
english: Vāsudeva also obtained eternal friendship with Pārtha; and the lord of gods, greatly pleased, granted him that boon at that time.

sanskrit: dattvā tābhyāṃ varaṃ prītaḥ saha devair marutpatiḥ hutāśanam anujñāpya jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ
english: Having joyfully granted the boon to both of them, the lord of the Maruts, together with the gods, took leave of the fire and returned to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: pāvakaś cāpi taṃ dāvaṃ dagdhvā samṛgapakṣiṇam ahāni pañca caikaṃ ca virarāma sutarpitaḥ
english: The fire too, having burned that forest along with its animals and birds, rested for five days and one more, fully satisfied.

sanskrit: jagdhvā māṃsāni pītvā ca medāṃsi rudhirāṇi ca yuktaḥ paramayā prītyā tāv uvāca viśāṃ pate
english: Having devoured the flesh and drunk the fat and blood, filled with supreme delight, he spoke to those two, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: yuvābhyāṃ puruṣāgryābhyāṃ tarpito 'smi yathāsukham anujānāmi vāṃ vīrau carataṃ yatra vāñchitam
english: Fire said: By the two of you, foremost among men, I have been satisfied to my full contentment. I grant you leave, O heroes; go wherever you desire.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau samanujñātau pāvakena mahātmanā arjuno vāsudevaś ca dānavaś ca mayas tathā
english: Thus were those two — Arjuna and Vāsudeva — granted leave by the great-souled fire, as was the demon Maya.

sanskrit: parikramya tataḥ sarve trayo 'pi bharatarṣabha ramaṇīye nadīkūle sahitāḥ samupāviśan
english: Then all three of them, O bull of the Bhāratas, having circumambulated the fire, sat down together on the pleasant bank of the river.
